fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. The LORD even hands them the words: “Ask for the ancient paths: ‘Where is the good way?’…” Then comes the promise, “Then walk in it, and you will find rest for your souls.”
Right, baker. The text says, “…‘We will not walk in it!’” That's like your GPS saying turn left and you answering out loud that you will not. The LORD shows them the good way, and they refuse it.

Yes, friend. The LORD says, “I appointed watchmen over you and said, ‘Listen for the sound of the ram’s horn.’…” Their answer: “We will not listen!” That's somebody telling the smoke alarm in advance to hush. The LORD gives them a warning to listen for, and they turn away from it.
That's it, baker. The LORD says, “Therefore hear, O nations, and learn, O congregations, what will happen to them.” Then He adds, “Hear, O earth!” That's a call for everybody to listen in.
Yes, baker. The LORD says, “Your burnt offerings are not acceptable; your sacrifices do not please Me.” Those are plain words, and I won't dress them up. The people's offerings do not please Him.
Yes, friend. The warning says, “Do not go out to the fields; do not walk the road.” The reason is right there with it: “For the enemy has a sword; terror is on every side.”

No king is mentioned in this verse, friend. The reason given is, “…for suddenly the destroyer will come upon us.” The call to mourn is compared to grief for an only son. It's the destroyer coming that they're called to mourn.
Good guess, friend, but it's not what the verse says. The LORD says, “All are hardened rebels, walking around as slanderers.” They're called His people just before that. So rebels is the word.
Clay isn't in this picture, friend. The picture uses ore, lead, bronze, iron and silver. The last verse says, “They are called rejected silver, because the LORD has rejected them.”
